title: Chamba rumal embroidery
summary: Chamba rumals come from the hill town of Chamba in Himachal Pradesh, India. On a square of fine unbleached cotton or muslin the design is first drawn in ink, then filled with silk in double satin stitch so the cloth looks identical on both faces.
howToPlay: Draw the outlines first: pick the ink and a shape, then touch a square.
Then fill the outlines with silk, one colour after another in the order shown on the plan.
Copy the drawing beside the cloth, then press Check.
rules: The panel mirrors left to right, so each shape you draw or fill is also worked on its partner square.
Draw before you fill: silk can only be laid on a square that already has its ink outline.
Silk colours are used in the order shown on the plan, and a square counts only when shape and colour both match.
heritageNote: Chamba rumals were embroidered by women of the hill region around Chamba and given as gifts at weddings and other family occasions. The finest pieces copied hill painting, and the craft is being kept alive by workshops and training centres.
